items.title: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (white paper)
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.locator: Principle: Accountability and governance, "Definition and explanation"
items.quote: ensure effective oversight of the supply and use of AI systems, with clear lines of accountability established across the AI life cycle
items.why: Source of the brief's quotation. One of the five cross-sector principles that UK regulators are asked to apply within their existing remits. Non-statutory: it creates no duty on a company directly. Published under the previous government; the page was last updated 3 August 2023.

items.title: AI Update
items.quote: management accountability and is relevant to the safe and responsible use of AI
items.why: How the financial regulator maps the accountability principle onto existing rules. In banks, insurers and Enhanced firms, technology systems normally sit with the Chief Operations function and risk controls with the Chief Risk function, and every activity must fall under some senior manager, so any use of AI does too. Core and Limited Scope firms are outside that part. Para 3.41: every senior manager has a Statement of Responsibilities and must take reasonable steps.

items.title: FS2/23: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (feedback statement)
items.publisher: Bank of England, Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority
items.locator: Paras 4.16-4.19 (questions 12 to 14); summary of key points
items.quote: Many respondents also said that firms need local owners to retain accountability over AI
items.why: What the industry told the regulators. DP5/22 received 54 responses. Most did not think a new prescribed responsibility for AI would help; some wanted a central AI function or committee, others accountability in business areas, and these were 'not seen as a mutually exclusive option'. A summary of responses only: the statement says it contains no policy proposals.

items.title: Supervisory Statement SS1/23: Model risk management principles for banks
items.publisher: Bank of England, Prudential Regulation Authority
items.locator: Principle 2.2 (SMF accountability for model risk management framework), PDF p.14-15
items.quote: An accountable SMF should be empowered to have overall oversight to ensure the effectiveness of the MRM framework.
items.why: A regulator requiring a named senior individual for a class of models. The firm's Statement of Responsibilities should reflect it, and model owners, developers and users stay responsible for individual models. Applies only to banks, building societies and designated investment firms with internal model approval.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
items.locator: Section on accountability and responsibility (practical recommendations)
items.quote: Nominate a senior responsible owner (SRO) who will be accountable for the use of AI in a specific project.
items.why: Government's instruction to its own departments. Also asks them to define responsibilities, accountability and liability across everyone involved, and to set them out in the contract where AI is bought. Public sector guidance, not binding on companies.

items.title: Use of artificial intelligence in government (HC 612)
items.quote: 24 of the 32 bodies with deployed AI told us that their AI use cases always or usually had a named accountable responsible owner
items.why: Source of the figure. From a survey of 87 government bodies carried out in autumn 2023, of which 32 had deployed AI. The same paragraph reports that only 15 said use cases were always or usually identified at organisational level before deployment. Government bodies only, self-reported, and now three years old.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 22A: Automated processing and significant decisions
items.quote: When considering whether there is meaningful human involvement in the taking of a decision, a person must consider, among other things
items.why: Where decision rights become a legal boundary. A decision with no meaningful human involvement is 'based solely on automated processing' and the safeguards regime applies. Substituted by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s.80(1); fully in force 5 February 2026 (S.I. 2026/82). The Article does not itself say what makes involvement meaningful.

items.title: Automated decision-making, including profiling (draft guidance): What does the UK GDPR say about ADM?
items.locator: Section on what meaningful human involvement means (criteria list)
items.quote: have discretion and authority to alter the decision
items.why: The regulator's reading of the test: the human should be active, not 'a token gesture', and should have discretion and authority to alter the decision. This is a draft updated on 31 March 2026 and the page still carries a consultation banner, so the wording may change. The word 'rubber-stamping' does not appear on this page.

items.title: OECD AI Principles: Accountability (Principle 1.5)
items.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
items.quote: AI actors should be accountable for the proper functioning of AI systems and for the respect of the above principles
items.why: The international baseline to which the UK has adhered. Accountability is tied to role and context, and actors are asked to ensure traceability of datasets, processes and decisions. A recommendation to governments, not a rule for companies. The page shows no publication date; the year given is the year the principles were adopted and was not confirmed on this page.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.
items.why: EU comparator for a UK business that deploys high-risk AI in the EU. Read on the European Commission's own copy, based on the consolidated text of 27 July 2026, because EUR-Lex returned an empty page. The 2026 amendments moved the high-risk dates; Article 113 on the same site was read, and the brief states no EU date.
